pack.name: Cyclohexane Reactor Ver 1 (R-101 · R-102 · R-103)
pack.desc: Benzene hydrogenation to cyclohexane: slurry reactors R-101 and R-102, trickle bed R-103, hydrogen recycle K-101 / V-104

FI-102.desc: R-102 liquid to R-103 through F-102

AI-103.desc: Product benzene, on-line GC (4-min cycle, 2-min sample delay; spec ≤ 10 ppm)

AI-104.desc: Product methylcyclopentane (isomer made when R-101 runs hot; spec ≤ 200 ppm)

FI-110.desc: Cyclohexane product to storage (HS-115 selects TK-106 on-spec or TK-107 slop)

AI-105.desc: Recycle gas hydrogen purity (rest CH4 / N2)

AI-100.desc: Loop oxygen (start-up purge analyzer; < 1 % before hydrogen)

FI-107.desc: Purge gas to fuel gas through HIC-107

FI-111.desc: LP steam exported from D-101 to the 3.5 bar g header

FI-108.desc: MP steam to the R-102 jacket (HEAT mode)

Conversion.desc: Overall conversion from the hydrogen balance

Heat released.desc: Reaction heat, all reactors (from H2 consumed)

TIC-101 − TI-100.desc: Difference of the two R-101 thermometers

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Product benzene creeping up (Cyclohexane Reactor Ver 1)
meta.sit: Unit lined out. The laboratory says product benzene was 2 ppm yesterday and 6 ppm this morning. Nothing has been changed on the board.

0.1.unit: Benzene + 3 H₂ → cyclohexane, 34.8 t/h of benzene in three reactors in series: R-101 slurry CSTR (200 °C, 30 bar g, Raney-Ni, about 98 % of the conversion, cooled by the E-101 pump-around raising LP steam and by boiling), R-102 slurry finishing reactor (160 °C on an MP steam jacket) and R-103, an adiabatic trickle bed of supported nickel. Hydrogen goes through all three in series to V-104 and back by K-101. Product FI-110 37.5 t/h to TK-106, benzene AI-103 2.0 ppm at design (spec ≤ 10 ppm), MCP AI-104 60 ppm (spec ≤ 200 ppm).

rows.what: Product benzene 2 ppm yesterday, 6 ppm this morning (laboratory)
On-line GC AI-103 2.0 ppm at load, 8.7 ppm and rising
No set point, mode or selector moved on the board

0.4.ctx: Day shift, unit lined out at design for weeks. No permits or maintenance on the reactor train today (assumed for the exercise). Product is sampled once per shift; the GC analyses every 4 minutes. Normal values from the snapshot design column.

R.1.p: R-101 does about 98 % of the work and owns the heat: the E-101 pump-around and boiling remove it, LP steam export FI-111 measures it. R-102 finishes to about 100 ppm benzene on a steam jacket held by TIC-102. R-103 is an adiabatic polishing bed of supported nickel that takes ≈100 ppm to ≈2 ppm. Hydrogen passes all three in series. The product spec is therefore owned by R-102 (what reaches R-103) and by R-103 (what fraction it lets through).

R.2.eq: x_product = x_R-102 out · (1 − X_R-103)     ΔT_bed = x · X · ṁ · ΔH / (M · ṁ · c_p)

sym.m: Benzene leaving R-102 = reaching R-103 (no analyser; ≈100 ppm at design)
Fraction of the benzene converted in R-103 (≈0.98 at design)
Liquid heat capacity, 2.38 kJ/(kg·K) from the model

“The GC is often wrong — probably nothing.”
The rise looks like a slow ramp, not a step

1.3.safn: R-101 200.0 °C (trip 220 °C); R-103 bed ≈158.6 °C (alarm 185 °C, trip 220 °C); no runaway sign
1.3.eqn: Catalyst condition unknown; nothing hot or vibrating
1.3.prodn: AI-103 8.7 ppm against the 10 ppm spec, rising ≈0.5 ppm/min: off spec in minutes (it was at 0:32:01)
1.3.ttl: Safety: far from every limit. Product: ≈2 min to the spec at the present rate

1.4.why: Nothing runs away and every instrument is needed for the tests; a shut-down costs a day of production and removes the evidence. Product quality is the only consequence, and slop routing contains it.
1.4.park: Prepared, then done at 0:32:30: HS-115 product to slop TK-107 as soon as AI-103 > 10 ppm. Rate cut with hydrogen in ratio only if the product cannot be recovered.

1.5.sp: A reduced, stable state that stops the consequence growing while we investigate: here the product goes to slop (and, if needed, benzene and hydrogen are cut together).
1.5.tc: A consequence (safety, environment, equipment) would arrive before the diagnosis is done unless we act now — not the case here; the product consequence is contained by slop routing.

1.6.p: Benzene removal in series: product benzene = benzene leaving R-102 × fraction R-103 lets through.

3.2.n: R-103 receives ≈100 ppm benzene in 10.41 kg/s of liquid. Converting 98 % of it releases 2.7 kW → ΔT = 0.11 °C. Even if R-103 stopped converting completely, the bed rise would fall by only ≈0.1 °C, inside the ±0.2 °C noise. The whole-train balances (conversion 100.08 %, heat released, H₂ consumed) cannot see a few ppm either. Only composition decides — the laboratory and AI-103.

rows.c: 100.08 % vs 100.00 % at design: the train converts as before (to 0.1 %)
lab 15.9 ppm at 0:30:30, GC 8.7 ppm: the lab leads by the GC delay on a rising value
0.05 °C vs 0.06 °C: below the thermocouple resolution — no information

3.5.tree:
TOP: product benzene > 10 ppm
 OR — more benzene reaches R-103
    OR — R-101 converts less (catalyst, hydrogen)
    OR — R-102 converts less (cold, steam, catalyst)
    OR — more benzene in the feed
 OR — R-103 lets a larger fraction through
    OR — activity loss
    OR — channelling / bypass
    OR — cold bed
 OR — the reading is wrong (GC, sample)
3.5.cut: Single-event cut sets: each branch alone can make the top event, so each needs its own test or evidence.

rows.st: “The GC is often wrong — probably nothing.”
rows.how: Tested by T-1: laboratory 15.9 ppm agrees with the GC
Tested by T-2 and FI-108: MP steam normal

rows.st: “Nothing has been changed on the board.”
rows.how: Event log: no OPER line before engagement

3.8.n: No operator or utility change before the rise. A slow ramp with no trigger points to something wearing out (activity, fouling, drift) rather than to an event.

3.10.n: R-101 and R-102 deliver ≈100 ppm to R-103 as at design; R-103 normally removes ≈98 % of it; product benzene is the only window on R-103 because its heat is below the thermocouple resolution.

3.11.n: The target (2.5) gains “or a dated plan”: if R-103 has lost activity the spec may be out of reach on line.

5.1.proof: Ev-1 with Ev-2 to Ev-6 (everything upstream at design); T-1 (laboratory agrees); T-2, T-3; T-4 (AI-103 kept rising with R-102 hotter)
5.1.mech: The supported-nickel catalyst of R-103 is losing activity → R-103 converts a smaller fraction of the ≈100 ppm benzene it receives from R-102 → product benzene climbs from 2 ppm to tens of ppm over half an hour → R-101, R-102, the hydrogen balance and the bed temperatures stay at design because R-103 converts only ≈100 ppm (≈0.1 °C, invisible) → only AI-103 and the laboratory see it. A hotter R-102 cuts what reaches R-103 only a little, so the product stays off spec; R-103 activity cannot be restored on line.

rows.opt: Product to slop (HS-115 → TK-107) while AI-103 > 10 ppm
Raise TIC-102 a few degrees (less benzene to R-103)
Cut the rate with hydrogen in ratio (more residence time in R-102 and R-103)
Change the R-103 catalyst at a planned shut-down

rows.step: Keep product on slop; laboratory sample every hour
Cut benzene 34.8 → 31 → 27 t/h with FIC-103 in ratio (done 0:53:30 and 0:55:30)
If any TI-107 bed > 175 °C or TIC-101 leaves 200 ± 3 °C: hold the rate and call the supervisor
MOC and work pack for the R-103 catalyst change (hydrogen-free entry, pyrophoric nickel handling)
Tell planning and the tank farm: reduced rate and slop receipts until the change

rows.act: HS-115 product to TK-106 (sales) / TK-107 (slop): TK106 → TK107

rows.pval: falls, perhaps below 10 ppm at 27 t/h

5.7.n: AI-103 fell from 43.4 to 24.3 ppm in 44 min at 27 t/h but stayed above 10 ppm: the rate cut slows the loss, it does not cure it. Product stays on slop; the R-103 catalyst change is brought forward. No R-103 inlet analyser — recommended in 6.1.

5.8.rule: Product benzene is the only early sign of R-103 activity: trend AI-103 daily, route to slop at 10 ppm without waiting, and never expect the bed temperatures to show it.

6.0.n: Every prediction under WH-5 came true; the outcome is poor because the cure needs a shut-down — the product could only be contained, not recovered on line.

rows.m: AI-103 HI switches HS-115 to TK-107 automatically (with a laboratory check or a time delay against a GC fault)
R-103 inlet benzene analyser (or a routine inlet sample) so its conversion is measured, not inferred
R-103 catalyst life tracked against throughput; change planned before end of life
Shift handover includes the AI-103 trend of the last 24 h

6.1.kpi: R-103 conversion (inlet sample vs AI-103), weekly; days to the planned catalyst change

rows.i: The catalyst change is planned, not an emergency
An automatic slop switch can send good product to slop on a GC fault

hz.sg: AI-103 HI → slop interlock; laboratory sample per shift

6.3.fut: A polishing reactor whose duty is too small to show on temperatures needs a composition measurement at its inlet; design it with the bed.

6.4.how: Rate cut against staying at full rate on slop: margin -7 392 instead of -9 419 $/h for 44 min (Profitability display) ≈ USD 1,486. Off-spec kept out of TK-106: ≈41 t of product — the claim avoided is not priced.

6.5.again: Wrote IS / IS NOT before any move; killed five hypotheses with samples, calls and local reads in under ten minutes; routed to slop at the spec without waiting; used one plant experiment to tell the last two apart.
6.5.never:
Never accept “the GC is wrong” without a laboratory sample.
Never raise R-101 temperature to fix product benzene (MCP and the boiling ceiling).
Never wait for a bed temperature to show a polishing-bed problem.

TIC-102 reads 159.92 °C against its design value 160.0 °C; TV-102 50.0 % (design 50.0); FI-108 MP steam 2.32 t/h (design 2.33) — no deviation (IS NOT candidate).

Hydrogen loop at design: AI-105 92.06 % (design 92.07); FI-106 make-up 31 974 Nm³/h (design 31 974); PIC-105 29.00 bar g.
AI-104 MCP 60 ppm on its design value 60 ppm.
Feed and R-102 hold-up at design: FIC-101 34.78 t/h (design 34.80); LIC-102 55.0 %; FI-102 20.9 t/h (design 20.9).

R-103 bed rise TI-107E − TI-106: mean 0.05 °C over the 8 min before 0:28:30 against 0.06 °C at design; thermocouple noise about ±0.2 °C.
Laboratory at 0:30:30: product benzene 15.9 ppm, MCP 60 ppm; benzene feed sulphur < 0.2 ppm; recycle gas H2 92.1 %, CH4+N2 7.9 %, O2 0.00 %; R-101 slurry: benzene 2.00 %, catalyst normal.
Utilities at 0:30:30: "CW supply normal; MP steam normal 10 bar g; LP header normal 3.5 bar g; BFW normal; N2 normal 8 bar g; instrument air normal."

hyp.cause: AI-103 reads high (analyser drift, calibration, sample line)
hyp.ifthen: If the GC is off, a laboratory sample of the same product reads near 2 ppm while AI-103 reads 8–15 ppm
hyp.fals: Laboratory agrees with AI-103 (allowing the GC delay)

hyp.cause: R-101 converts less (slurry catalyst poisoned, too little hydrogen)
hyp.ifthen: If R-101 converted less, its heat would fall: FIC-104 duty and the LP steam export FI-111 drop, and the slurry benzene rises above 2 %
hyp.fals: FI-111 and E-101 duty at design; slurry benzene 2 %

hyp.cause: R-102 colder than it reads / MP steam to the jacket short
hyp.ifthen: If R-102 ran cold, TIC-102 would sit below 160 °C or TV-102 wide open with FI-108 low, and the utilities desk would know of an MP steam problem
hyp.fals: TIC-102 160 °C with TV-102 ≈50 %, FI-108 and TT-102 at design, MP steam normal

hyp.cause: Hydrogen partial pressure low (make-up purity, purge, loop pressure)
hyp.ifthen: If the loop lost hydrogen partial pressure every reactor would slow: AI-105 or PIC-105 down, R-101 duty down, MCP up
hyp.fals: AI-105, PIC-105 and the make-up purity at design

hyp.cause: R-103 passes a larger fraction of the benzene it receives (finishing catalyst losing activity, channelling)
hyp.ifthen: If R-103 converts less, product benzene rises while everything upstream stays at design; the bed rise cannot show it (≈0.1 °C at design); a hotter R-102 lowers the product only a little
hyp.key: AI-103 ↑ with R-101, R-102 and the loop flat; small response to TIC-102 +5 °C
hyp.fals: AI-103 falls back below spec when R-102 is made hotter, or the bed rise moves

hyp.cause: R-102 sends more benzene to R-103 than its indicators show (R-102 converting less at 160 °C)
hyp.ifthen: If R-102 converted less, raising TIC-102 by 5 °C would cut the benzene reaching R-103 a lot, and AI-103 would fall clearly within ≈20 min

hyp.cause: More benzene or impurities in the feed (rate up, sulphur)
hyp.ifthen: If the feed changed, FIC-101 would be above 34.8 t/h or the feed sulphur would be up, and R-101 would show it first
hyp.fals: FIC-101 at design and feed sulphur < 0.2 ppm
